title: "Forty hedging whips at Hexham"
excerpt: "Last week we planted 40 bare-root hawthorn and hazel whips at the Hexham garden, the start of a hedge that will knit together in about three years."
body: |
  Last week we planted 40 bare-root hedging whips at the Hexham garden, a mix of hawthorn and hazel.

  For now they look like a row of sticks. Bare-root plants go in while they are dormant, which gives their roots the winter to settle before spring. In about three years they will knit together into a proper hedge.

  If you have a hedge, a gap or a new bed in mind, winter is the time to plant it. Get in touch to book a winter planting visit.
